rubrics.criterion: Every device-level member of the input-sequence builder abstractions (typing key press/release, pointer button press/release, pointer movement, wheel scrolling, and the press-release shorthands) is declared on an abstraction implemented only by the input sources that genuinely queue that kind of event; no input source retains such a member that it satisfies by discarding its arguments and returning the builder unchanged, and no source inherits that kind of member as a shared trait default.
rubrics.rationale: This is the central obligation of this case: the injected state hands every source type the same device vocabulary regardless of which device it drives, with do-nothing bodies where the source cannot perform the event. Grading must confirm the grouping is per capability, not that it matches any particular trait naming or file layout.

rubrics.criterion: Vendor-routing members (per-command URL override, per-command transport headers) are carried only by commands that genuinely participate in vendor routing: the crate's general command contract no longer requires them from every implementor, and the internal wrapper for standard WebDriver commands no longer provides them as empty answers. The repair is acceptable whether the vendor surface is removed together with its integration or kept as an opt-in capability attached only to genuinely vendor-routed commands.
rubrics.rationale: The second manifestation of the same relationship sits in the command plumbing, where a hypothetical capability became a blanket obligation for every command including downstream implementors of the public contract. Both a removal and a coherent opt-in re-home resolve it.

rubrics.criterion: The members that genuinely apply to every input source type (contributing a pause tick, chaining one raw action payload into the sequence) remain declared on the shared abstraction and stay available on every source, including the null source that contributes only pauses.
rubrics.rationale: A correct split redistributes only the device-specific obligations. Splitting off more than the device members - or hollowing out the genuinely universal composition surface - would not be a sound refactor, and this item protects the universal part of the boundary.

rubrics.criterion: The session's request-issuing path was brought in step with the command-surface change: it no longer consults vendor-routing members on commands that do not carry them (no dangling call sites or unreachable branches for the removed consult), and request URL derivation goes through the endpoint path for every command that reaches it.
rubrics.rationale: The vendor consult was wired into the function that turns a command into an HTTP request, so the two must move together. This is the coupled consumer of the reorganized contract and must be graded as its own obligation rather than being implied by the trait-level change.

rubrics.criterion: All capabilities the browser-facing exercise drives (typing characters through the keyboard source, moving the pointer and tapping through a pointer source, and the press-release shorthands) remain reachable through the crate's public item set after the change, regardless of which module or abstraction each one now lives on.
rubrics.rationale: The re-homing can leave a capability technically present but unreachable from outside the crate (for example by narrowing visibility). End-to-end exercises live inside the crate tree, so they cannot by themselves prove public reachability; this item verifies the published API boundary.

rubrics.criterion: The end-to-end browser exercise that arrived with this work was migrated to the post-change abstractions rather than worked around: its import list and call sites go through the new per-capability grouping while still driving the same page interactions (typing into the text input, moving and clicking the alert button, and asserting the resulting page state).
rubrics.rationale: The exercise is the only test-level consumer of the new builder surface and pins its ergonomics. A repair that leaves it driven by the old flat grouping, or reduces what it exercises, silently weakens the acceptance boundary.

rubrics.criterion: Production sources still contain comments or documentation that describe the placeholder arrangement: trait or impl documentation asserting that sources which do not produce an event kind accept its arguments without queueing an action, or per-body notes explaining that arguments are accepted and dropped so that shared builder chains stay fluent.
rubrics.rationale: These text fragments are shipped with the placeholder bodies themselves and describe code that a sound repair removes. Leaving them behind misleads future maintainers about what the builders do, so presence of any such text fails this item.

rubrics.criterion: Obsolete fragments of the removed grouping were left behind: empty or vestigial impl blocks, member groups that remain defined on a type that no longer has any purpose for them, blanket forwarding implementations left in place for an abstraction that no longer exists, or use-declarations that still name abstractions absent from the post-change structure.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state added forwarding conveniences, per-surface declarations, and import entries; a complete repair removes the ones the new design no longer needs instead of abandoning them. Vestigial structure is compile-clean clutter that this item targets.

rubrics.criterion: The end-to-end browser exercise was deleted, commented out, marked ignored, or had its assertions weakened to dodge the required migration (for example asserting nothing about the typed text or the raised alert), rather than being updated to the post-change abstractions.
rubrics.rationale: Deleting or defusing the pinning exercise is the cheapest way to make a weakened repair look green, and a plain test-count comparison will not catch it. This item makes that specific gaming path a graded failure.

rubrics.criterion: Capabilities were dropped instead of re-homed: after the change, typing characters on the keyboard source, pressing/releasing a pointer button, moving the pointer, scrolling by deltas, or the press-release shorthand is no longer expressible through a builder-style chained call on a source type that produces that kind of event (only through falling back to raw action payloads).
rubrics.rationale: The expected failure mode is that the split is done by subtraction: removing the device members entirely 'solves' the placeholder problem while taking away the advertised fluent entry points. Falling back fully to composing raw payload variants is the regression this item catches.

rubrics.criterion: The wire-level semantics of an input sequence changed as part of the reorganization: pause ticks or the ordering of chained actions within the converted payload sequence were altered, or the conversion from a source type into the action-sequence payload format was reworked such that the same builder chain now produces a different sequence than before the change.
rubrics.rationale: Reorganizing where members live must not disturb tick composition, which the WebDriver protocol session timing and action bursts depend on. A silent reorder or lost tick would pass many test setups, so it is called out as its own graded failure mode.

rubrics.criterion: Request-path behavior outside the two reorganized areas changed: endpoint resolution for ordinary commands, user-agent or credential header attachment, or new-session/legacy classification of commands no longer matches the pre-change request behavior.
rubrics.rationale: The vendor consult was inserted in the middle of an existing request-construction routine. While removing it, a solver can accidentally alter adjacent behavior; this item verifies the rest of the transport flow was left intact.
